title: Introduce RBACv2 constraint templates and KMS consistency checker for region-affinity compliance
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: Customers operating under strict residency rules asked for a declarative way to express RBAC constraints that must also be enforced against KMS key location and audit headers. This PR introduces a first-class 'constraint template' concept for RBACv2 and a KMS consistency checker that validates outgoing crypto calls against claim-based region pins.

What this does: adds a templating layer for common constraint patterns (e.g., require-tenant-region, deny-operator-crosszone) plus a lightweight KMS call preflight that asserts the chosen CMK region matches the request's residency claim and produces enriched audit annotations when mismatches are detected. Templates are pluggable so later policies (retention, export-control) can reuse the same building blocks.

Design summary: the constraint templates are YAML manifests compiled into policy fragments by the rbacv2 engine at start-up; templates support parameterization (scope=service|tenant, mode=deny|warn|enforce, key_selector). The KMS consistency checker is implemented as an interceptor in pkg/kms/client_interceptor.go that checks key metadata (region tag, provider) against request claims emitted by the edge auth layer. When enforcement is configured as 'warn' we emit audit enrichment messages and metric labels rather than rejecting requests.

Compatibility and rollout: default behavior is no-op for existing customers. New template manifests are staged behind a feature flag (rbacv2.constraint_templates) and the KMS checker is enabled for a subset of regions (eu-west-1, us-west-2) during the canary. We provide a migration CLI to convert ad-hoc RBAC rules into templated forms.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for template compilation, end-to-end integration tests simulating mismatched CMK region + residency claim, and a litmus test for audit envelope enrichment. Benchmarks show ~0.6ms median added latency on a cold path for KMS-prefetch; warm path impact is sub-ms.

Checklist:
- [x] Template schema and compiler implemented
- [x] KMS interceptor and metadata lookup implemented
- [x] Audit enrichment hook wired to audit-proxy
- [x] Integration tests and CI coverage
- [x] Documentation and quickstart for operators

Related: ENG-8123 (policy infra), ENG-8299 (kms metadata cache), SUP-1023 (customer request), internal RFC: rfc/rbac/constraint-templates.md

Notes for reviewers: focus on failure modes in the kms interceptor (network error vs. metadata mismatch) and on the security implications of 'warn' mode. I included a short compatibility shim to avoid rejecting calls from legacy SDKs that don't send residency claims: in that case we log a high-severity audit event but do not deny by default.
